# Convert AVIF to JPG

- Route: `/tools/convert-avif-to-jpg`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `image`
- Slug: `convert-avif-to-jpg`

## Summary

Turn modern AVIF images into universally compatible JPG files for apps and sites that don’t accept AVIF. (Image tools)

## Details

AVIF is a cutting-edge image format that produces tiny files, but plenty of apps, editors, and upload forms still can’t open it. Media Manipulator converts AVIF to JPG so your image works everywhere. Pick a quality and download.
### What it does
- Converts AVIF images to standard JPG.
- Flattens any transparency onto a background, since JPG has no alpha.
- Lets you choose JPG quality for the size/fidelity balance you want.
- Produces a JPG that opens on any device or app.
### How to use it
1. Upload AVIF: Drop in a .avif image.
2. Pick JPG quality: 85 is a balanced default.
3. Encode JPG: ImageMagick decodes AVIF (libaom/libheif) and writes a JPG.
4. Download JPG: Save a universally compatible .jpg.
### Supported formats
- Input: avif
- Output: jpg
- AVIF decoding requires ImageMagick with an AVIF delegate on the server. Transparency is flattened in JPG output.
### Technical details
- AVIF decoding relies on ImageMagick built with an AVIF delegate (libaom or libheif). If the server lacks AVIF support, the tool returns a clear error.
- AVIF supports transparency; when converting to JPG, transparent areas are flattened because JPG has no alpha channel. Use AVIF → PNG to keep transparency.
- Quality 85–90 keeps the JPG visually identical to the AVIF for most images.
### Use cases
- Saving web images: Convert an AVIF you downloaded into a usable JPG.
- App compatibility: Open an AVIF in software that lacks AVIF support.
- Uploads: Meet a form that only accepts JPG.
- Printing: Produce a JPG for a photo lab.
### FAQ
Q: How do I convert AVIF to JPG for free?
A: Upload your .avif image above, pick a quality, and click convert. You get a standard .jpg back.
Q: Why can’t I open AVIF files?
A: AVIF is a newer format; many apps, editors, and websites haven’t added support yet. Converting to JPG makes the image open everywhere.
Q: What about transparency?
A: JPG has no transparency, so transparent AVIF areas are flattened onto a background. If you need to keep transparency, use the AVIF → PNG tool.
Q: Will I lose quality?
A: At quality 85–90 the JPG looks essentially identical to the AVIF for most images.
